newsitem.title: UK: Fish oil could be dangerous, environmentalists say.
newsitem.headline: Fish oil could be dangerous, environmentalists say.

text.p: Some fish oil supplements such as cod liver oil could be contaminated with dangerous levels of toxic chemicals, environmentalists said on Monday.
But Britain's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAFF) said a study it commissioned into the supplements showed they were safe.

Fish oil supplements are becomingly increasingly popular because of evidence they can help cut rates of heart disease and confer other benefits. But environmentalists have said they could also deliver hidden poisons because of the growing pollution of oceans and lakes.
"Contaminated cod liver oil takes school children and toddlers over the toxic safety threshold," Friends of the Earth said in a statement.

It said significant levels of dioxin and PCBs had been found in cod liver oil. The World Health Organisation says both can cause cancer and governments in many countries go to great lengths to make sure people do not get exposed to either chemical.
But a spokeswoman for MAFF said the report, published last month, found the levels in supplements it had tested were safe.
"The conclusion by the Committee on Toxicology was that intakes of dioxins and PCBs were unlikely to pose a risk," she said.

Michael Warhurst, a biochemist specialising in the effects of such chemicals and a campaigner for Friends of the Earth, said the levels found in the report exceeded those recommended by the World Health Organisation as safe.
"The government accepts the WHO recommendations yet says these levels are safe," he said.

"We would say there should be proper advice from government about giving something that is not essential to children." He also said the government should name which supplements had the highest levels.
People could get the health benefits of fish oil without the risk, he added. Flaxseed oil, canola (rapeseed) oil and soy oil are all good sources of the omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids.

Companies that make the supplements had no immediate comment. "We are still waiting for a copy of the research," said a spokeswomen for Boots Co Plc, the British pharmacy and health and beauty retailer.
Warhurst said the chemicals, released into the oceans by industry, were attracted to the fat in the bodies of fish. The fat is pressed out of the fish as oil by companies making fish-oil supplements.
Liver oil, he said, was particularly dangerous as the liver is the organ that works to filter out foreign chemicals from the body.
Warhurst said children who took one daily capsule of cod liver oil could exceed the WHO's recommended safe maximum dose of dioxin. Pregnant women who took the supplement could damage the foetus.
"These chemicals are known to be particularly associated with disrupting development," he said. The reproductive system was especially vulnerable
"The key area is during pregnancy and pre-puberty," Warhurst said. Adults were at less risk but could still double their exposure, he added.
